caption_used: Training loss curves over iterations for Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four SepLLM configurations. All models start with loss values exceeding 3.4 and converge as training progresses to 140,000 iterations. The Vanilla model achieves the lowest final loss at approximately 2.45, while StrmLLM (n=64) converges to roughly 2.60, showing a notable gap from the SepLLM variants. Among the SepLLM configurations, the H/T variant reaches the lowest loss at approximately 2.49, with SepLLM (n=128) settling at approximately 2.55, slightly above both the base SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) which converge near 2.51-2.52. The most rapid decrease in loss occurs within the first 20,000 iterations for all models, after which convergence slows considerably.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This line plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for five different model configurations: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), and four variants of SepLLM (n=64, n=64, H, n=64, H/T, and n=128). The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents the loss, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Each model is represented by a distinct colored line with a solid style and no markers: Vanilla (purple), StrmLLM (n=64) (blue), SepLLM (n=64) (orange), SepLLM (n=64, H) (green), SepLLM (n=64, H/T) (red), and SepLLM (n=128) (dark blue). All models start with loss values above 3.3 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline in loss during the first 20,000 iterations. The loss then decreases more gradually as training progresses. At 140,000 iterations, the Vanilla model reaches a loss of approximately 2.45, StrmLLM (n=64) stabilizes around 2.60, SepLLM (n=64) and SepLLM (n=64, H) converge to approximately 2.51–2.52, SepLLM (n=64, H/T) reaches about 2.49, and SepLLM (n=128) settles at approximately 2.55. The plot includes a grid for easier reading and a legend positioned in the upper right corner.
